title: Dust masses of young disks: constraining the initial solid reservoir for planet formation
question: Do embedded Class 0/I disks in Perseus contain enough dust to explain the solid content of the most massive exoplanets, and what efficiency is needed?

what.value: 1.3 mm flux densities of 25 Perseus disks

evidence.quote: We also use the flux densities of 25 disks published in (cite: Tobin2018) which were observed at 1.3 mm

what.value: VLA 9 mm fluxes corrected for free-free emission

evidence.quote: We use the 9 mm fluxes corrected for the free-free emission for further analysis.

evidence.loc: ALMA Class 0/I disk masses for different star-forming regions
evidence.quote: In Fig. [3](#fig:cdplots_per_ori) we show the cumulative distribution of disks observed with ALMA for Orion (cite: Tobin2020) and for Perseus.
The exoplanet systems masses were obtained from the exoplanet.eu database (cite: Schneider2011).

recipe.goal: measure disk fluxes with Gaussian fits
recipe.method: imfit with compact Gaussian plus optional broad 3" envelope Gaussian; compact component taken as disk
key_parameters: Envelope Gaussian added in 31 of 51 targets; initial broad size 3"
assumptions: Compact Gaussian flux equals disk flux

recipe.goal: compare ALMA and VLA fluxes and derive spectral index and beta
recipe.method: Linear fit of fluxes with lmfit; alpha between 1 mm and 9 mm; beta = (alpha-2)(1+Delta); optically thin subsample where alpha_VLA/ALMA - alpha_VLA <= 0.4
M = D^2 F / (kappa B(T)), T=30 K; CDFs with survival analysis including upper limits; medians at 0.5 probability
key_parameters: kappa_9mm = 0.28 cm2/g (DIANA); kappa_1.3mm = 2.3 cm2/g; for Orion comparison kappa_1.3mm = 0.9

recipe.goal: compare to exoplanet solids and derive formation efficiency
recipe.method: Exoplanet systems (>=1 planet >0.3 MJ) normalized to 18% of population; solid mass via Thorngren2016; efficiency = ratio of exoplanet to disk dust mass at same CDF level
key_parameters: 0.3 MJ planet solid fraction 27.8 Mearth set at 18% of CDF

answer_key.quantity: Slope of ALMA vs VLA flux correlation

evidence.loc: Comparison of the integrated fluxes between 1 and 9 mm

answer_key.quantity: Mean spectral index of optically thin subsample (23 sources)

evidence.loc: Comparison of the integrated fluxes between 1 and 9 mm
evidence.quote: The mean spectral index of those sources is 2.5, which means that $\beta \sim 0.5$.

answer_key.quantity: Median dust mass from VLA, Class 0 / Class I

evidence.quote: The median masses measured from the 9 mm observations are 158 M${_\oplus}$ for Class 0 and 52 M${_\oplus}$ for Class I

answer_key.quantity: Median dust mass lower limits from ALMA, Class 0 / Class I

evidence.quote: is 47 M${_\oplus}$ and 12 M${_\oplus}$ for Class 0 and Class I disks, respectively

answer_key.quantity: Median Perseus vs Orion dust mass (kappa=0.9, 30 K), Class 0

evidence.loc: ALMA Class 0/I disk masses for different star-forming regions
evidence.quote: 67 M$_\oplus$ versus 131 M$_\oplus$ in Perseus, but is remarkably similar for Class I: 25 M$_\oplus$ versus 33 M$_\oplus$.

answer_key.quantity: Planet formation efficiency from VLA masses, Class 0 / Class I

evidence.loc: Comparison of young disk dust masses with the solids in exoplanetary systems
evidence.quote: the efficiency of planet formation would have to be on the order of 15% for Class 0 and 34% for Class I

answer_key.quantity: Efficiency from ALMA lower-limit masses, Class 0 / Class I

evidence.loc: Comparison of young disk dust masses with the solids in exoplanetary systems
evidence.quote: the efficiency of forming planets in the Class 0 phase would be on the order of 33%. The efficiency of the Class I phase would be on the order of 72%.

score_reason: Public data and clear recipe, but imaging details and tabulated fluxes missing and exoplanet step loosely specified.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, mostly simple flux fits and mass formula with numeric medians.
